Adjust the number of internal faces $|I|$ to be drawn in the current frame to maintain the target frame rate.
Using the Primary LUT in this state causes visual artifacts.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of faces rasterized.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for the mesh faces, the k-buffer (size $k$ per pixel), and two LUTs.
- **Strengths:** Operates on mesh faces rather than cells, resulting in fewer rasterizations ($2n$ triangles for $n$ tetrahedra) compared to projected tetrahedra ($3.4n$).
This method was developed by Steve Callahan as part of his Master's thesis research on the k-buffer and its applications to volume rendering.
It builds directly on the Hardware-Assisted Visibility Sorting (HAVS) algorithm described in Chapter 4 of the same work.
